records.heading: The burial and the guard at the tomb

records.source: οὗτος προσελθὼν τῷ Πιλάτῳ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
records.gloss: This one having gone to the Pilate asked for the body of the Jesus.
pieces: He went to Pilate and requested Jesus's body.

L.58: He went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.

R.58: Joseph went to Pilate and asked him for Jesus's body.

decisions.choice: asked for the body: permission was needed
alternatives: the body would have been given anyway
decisions.reason: Romans often left the bodies of the crucified on the cross or threw them in a common grave. To ask for the body of a man executed for rebellion took courage (Mark 15:43).

decisions.choice: Joseph
decisions.reason: Readable names Joseph.

records.source: τότε ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἐκέλευσεν ἀποδοθῆναι.
records.gloss: Then the Pilate ordered to be given.
pieces: Pilate then ordered that it be handed over to him.

L.58: Then Pilate ordered [it] to be given [to him].

R.58: Pilate gave orders for the body to be given to Joseph.

decisions.choice: to be given: to be handed over to Joseph
alternatives: to be given back to the family
decisions.reason: The verb means to give over or give back. Pilate releases the body to Joseph.

decisions.choice: the body; to Joseph
decisions.reason: Readable says what was given and to whom.

records.source: καὶ λαβὼν τὸ σῶμα ὁ Ἰωσὴφ ἐνετύλιξεν αὐτὸ σινδόνι καθαρᾷ, καὶ ἔθηκεν αὐτὸ ἐν τῷ καινῷ αὐτοῦ μνημείῳ ὃ ἐλατόμησεν ἐν τῇ πέτρᾳ, καὶ προσκυλίσας λίθον μέγαν τῇ θύρᾳ τοῦ μνημείου ἀπῆλθεν.
records.gloss: And having taken the body the Joseph wrapped it in a linen cloth clean, \v 60 and placed it in the new of him tomb which he had hewn in the rock, and having rolled a stone great to the door of the tomb he went away.
pieces: Joseph took the body and wound a clean linen sheet around it.
Then he placed it in the new tomb he had carved in the rock for himself, rolled a great stone across the doorway of the tomb, and went away.

L.59: And Joseph took the body and wrapped it in clean linen cloth
L.60: and laid it in his own new tomb, which he had cut in the rock; and having rolled a great stone to the door of the tomb, he went away.

R.59: Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean cloth made of linen.
R.60: He put the body in his own new tomb, which had been cut into the rock. Then he rolled a big stone in front of the opening to close the tomb, and he went away.

decisions.choice: clean linen: a fresh linen sheet for burial
decisions.reason: The dead were wrapped in linen cloth. A clean, new cloth showed honor to the dead.

decisions.choice: his own new tomb cut in the rock: a family tomb no one had used
decisions.reason: Wealthy families in Jerusalem had tombs cut into the rock, with shelves for bodies inside. Luke 23:53 and John 19:41 say no one had yet been laid in it.

decisions.choice: a great stone at the door: a large stone that closed the entrance
decisions.reason: Such stones were often round and rolled in a groove across the doorway. It will be sealed and guarded (27:66) and rolled away (28:2).

decisions.choice: it, for the body
decisions.reason: The Greek pronoun is neuter and refers to the body. It is not a pronoun for Jesus himself, so it takes no setting.

records.source: ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ Μαριὰμ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ ἡ ἄλλη Μαρία καθήμεναι ἀπέναντι τοῦ τάφου.
records.gloss: Was then there Mary the Magdalene and the other Mary sitting opposite the tomb.
pieces: Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary too, seated facing the tomb.

L.61: And Mary the Magdalene was there, and the other Mary, sitting opposite the tomb.

R.61: Mary from Magdala and the other Mary were there. They were sitting across from the tomb.

decisions.choice: the other Mary: the mother of James and Joseph
decisions.reason: She is the second Mary named in 27:56. The two women will come back to the tomb in 28:1.

decisions.choice: sitting opposite the tomb: they saw where he was laid
decisions.reason: The women see the place of burial, so they know which tomb they find empty (28:1, 6).

decisions.choice: Mary: a second spelling of the same name in the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT spells Mary Magdalene's name in a slightly different form here than in 27:56. It is the same name and the same woman.

records.source: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον, ἥτις ἐστὶν μετὰ τὴν παρασκευήν, συνήχθησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι πρὸς Πιλᾶτον λέγοντες· Κύριε, ἐμνήσθημεν ὅτι ἐκεῖνος ὁ πλάνος εἶπεν ἔτι ζῶν· Μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἐγείρομαι·
records.gloss: The then next day, which is after the Preparation, were gathered together the chief priests and the Pharisees before Pilate \v 63 saying, Sir, we remembered that that deceiver said while living, After three days I am raised.
pieces: On the following day, the one after the day of Preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees came together to Pilate.
"Sir," they said, "we have remembered something that impostor said while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still alive: 'After three days I will be raised.'

L.62: And on the next day, which is after the Preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered before Pilate
L.63: and said, "Sir, we have remembered that that deceiver said while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still living, 'After three days I am raised.'

R.62: The next day was the Sabbath, the day after Preparation Day. The leading priests and the Pharisees went to Pilate together.
R.63: They said, "Sir, we remember something that liar said while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still alive. He said, 'After three days I will come back to life.'

decisions.choice: the day after the Preparation: the Sabbath
decisions.reason: Preparation was the day before the Sabbath, the Friday on which Jesus died. The next day was the Sabbath itself.

decisions.choice: deceiver: one who leads people astray
decisions.reason: The word means one who misleads. Jesus warned that false messiahs would lead many astray (24:4-5, 24); his enemies call him one.

decisions.choice: I am raised: the present for a sure future; it can mean I rise or I am raised
decisions.reason: Jesus foretold that he would be raised on the third day (16:21; 17:23; 20:19). The leaders quote the promise to guard against it.

decisions.choice: Sir: a polite address
alternatives: Lord, as a confession of faith
decisions.reason: The word is the same as "Lord", but spoken to Pilate it is a title of respect.

decisions.choice: The next day was the Sabbath
decisions.reason: Readable says which day it was. Pronouns for Jesus take the deity_pronoun setting even in his enemies' words; a pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plain.

records.source: κέλευσον οὖν ἀσφαλισθῆναι τὸν τάφον ἕως τῆς τρίτης ἡμέρας, μήποτε ἐλθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ κλέψωσιν αὐτὸν καὶ εἴπωσιν τῷ λαῷ· Ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ ἔσται ἡ ἐσχάτη πλάνη χείρων τῆς πρώτης.
records.gloss: Command therefore to be secured the tomb until the third day, lest having come the disciples of him they steal him and say to the people, He was raised from the dead, and will be the last deception worse than the first.
pieces: Give the command, then, to have the tomb guarded securely until the third day. If not, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples could come, take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away by stealth, and announce to the people, 'He has been raised from the dead.' And this final fraud would do more harm than the first one."

L.64: So command that the tomb be made secure until the third day, so that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples do not come and steal {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and say to the people, 'He has been raised from the dead,' and the last deception will be worse than the first."

R.64: So please give orders for the tomb to be guarded until the third day. If you do not, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers might come and steal {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body. Then they would tell the people, 'He has come back from death!' This last lie would be even worse than the first one."

decisions.choice: the last deception, the first: a report of resurrection would be worse than his claims while alive
decisions.reason: The first deception, as the leaders see it, is Jesus's own claim to be the Messiah and the Son of God (26:63-64). The last would be the news that he rose.

decisions.choice: until the third day: counting the day of his death as the first
decisions.reason: The third day was the day after the Sabbath, the day of 28:1.

decisions.choice: steal him: carry off his body
decisions.reason: The leaders speak of Jesus himself, though they mean the body.

decisions.choice: his body
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the leaders mean his body. The pronoun still refers to Jesus and takes the setting.

records.source: ἔφη αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Ἔχετε κουστωδίαν· ὑπάγετε ἀσφαλίσασθε ὡς οἴδατε.
records.gloss: Said to them the Pilate, You have a guard; go, make secure as you know.
pieces: Pilate told them, "You may have a guard. Go and secure it in whatever way you think best."

L.65: Pilate said to them, "You have a guard; go, make [it] as secure as you know [how]."

R.65: Pilate said, "You can have some soldiers. Go and guard the tomb the best way you know."

decisions.choice: you have a guard: take a guard of soldiers
alternatives: you have your own temple guard
decisions.reason: The verb can be a statement or a command. The guards later report to the chief priests (28:11), which could suit the temple police; but the leaders promise to keep them out of trouble with the governor (28:14), which suits Roman soldiers.

decisions.choice: guard: a group of soldiers on watch
decisions.reason: The word comes from Latin and names a detachment of guards.

decisions.choice: You may have (B); You can have (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the reading as a command or permission, which the meaning decision marks as uncertain.

records.source: οἱ δὲ πορευθέντες ἠσφαλίσαντο τὸν τάφον σφραγίσαντες τὸν λίθον μετὰ τῆς κουστωδίας.
records.gloss: They then having gone made secure the tomb having sealed the stone with the guard.
pieces: They went and sealed the stone, and with the guard in place they made the tomb secure.

L.66: So they went and made the tomb secure, sealing the stone along with the guard.

R.66: So they went to the tomb. They put a seal on the stone, and they left soldiers there to guard it.

decisions.choice: sealing the stone: a cord or wax seal, so that tampering would show
decisions.reason: A seal across the stone and the rock would be broken if anyone moved it (compare Daniel 6:17).

decisions.choice: with the guard: by posting the guard as well
decisions.reason: The tomb was made secure in two ways: by the seal and by the soldiers.
